div.head: ECf 32 E 4
div.ab: Maluerunt enim manere in regno isto quam in terra eorum propria. Terra uero eorum arida est et montuosa et sterilis, et non sunt ibi segetes nisi per loca. Ista uero opulenta est et fertilis, et crescunt hic segetes et cetera uniuersa. Qua de causa sepius per uices gesta sunt bella atrocissima inter Anglos et Norwegienses, et interfecti sunt uiri multi et ineffabiles et ex utraque parte sepius innumerabiles gladio ceciderunt.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 660 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 E …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
div.ab: For they preferred to remain in this kingdom rather than in their own land. For their land is dry and mountainous and barren, and there are no crops there except in places. But this is rich and fertile, and crops and all other things grow here. For which reason most fierce wars have very often been waged by turns between the English and the Norwegians, and many men past telling have been slain, and on both sides very often men without number have fallen by the sword.
